full_text_en:
Luo Guoqing, Li Renguang, Chen Yaokun, Liang Hongjie, and Zhao Jilin — Bribery Case

Defendant: Luo Guoqing, male, 52 years old, formerly engineer of the Construction and Installation Company of Guangzhou Heavy Machinery Factory, Guangdong Province. Arrested on September 20, 1985.

Defendant: Li Renguang, male, 51 years old, formerly manager of the Construction and Installation Company of Guangzhou Heavy Machinery Factory, Guangdong Province. Arrested on September 23, 1985.

Defendant: Chen Yaokun, male, 52 years old, formerly deputy manager of the Construction and Installation Company of Guangzhou Heavy Machinery Factory, Guangdong Province. Arrested on September 26, 1985.

Defendant: Liang Hongjie, male, 42 years old, formerly assistant engineer of the Construction and Installation Company of Guangzhou Heavy Machinery Factory, Guangdong Province. Arrested on September 20, 1985.

Defendant: Zhao Jilin, male, 38 years old, formerly assistant engineer of the Construction and Installation Company of Guangzhou Heavy Machinery Factory, Guangdong Province. Arrested on December 3, 1985.

During the period when Defendants Luo Guoqing, Li Renguang, Chen Yaokun, Liang Hongjie, and Zhao Jilin were in charge of infrastructure projects at the Guangzhou Heavy Machinery Factory, they exploited their positions and used the method of collecting "kickbacks" to extensively demand and accept bribes from the construction units undertaking the factory's infrastructure projects. The facts are as follows:

1. In August 1983, the Guangzhou Heavy Machinery Factory commenced the construction of Project No. 82-5. Defendant Luo Guoqing conspired with Defendants Liang Hongjie and Zhao Jilin, and with the consent of Defendants Li Renguang and Chen Yaokun, demanded a "kickback" from the No. 204 Construction Team of Qingyuan County No. 2 Construction Engineering Company, which was undertaking this project. Subsequently, Luo Guoqing and Liang Hongjie handled the collection of RMB 46,000 as a "kickback" from the company. Luo Guoqing distributed RMB 12,000 to Li Renguang, and RMB 7,000 each to Chen Yaokun, Liang Hongjie, Zhao Jilin, and himself. In addition, RMB 2,000 each was given to project introducers Qin Hongtian, Liu Man, and Chen Jinbin (these three were dealt with in separate cases).

2. In November 1983, the No. 204 Construction Team of Qingyuan County No. 2 Construction Engineering Company continued to undertake the construction of the plate warehouse project of Guangzhou Heavy Machinery Factory. Luo Guoqing collected a "kickback" of RMB 14,000, distributing RMB 8,000 to Li Renguang and keeping RMB 6,000 for himself.

3. In April 1984, the No. 204 Construction Team of Qingyuan County No. 2 Construction Engineering Company again undertook three projects at Guangzhou Heavy Machinery Factory: the mud pump test stand, the boring machine foundation, and the X-ray inspection room of the riveting and welding workshop. Luo Guoqing demanded a "kickback" of RMB 4,500, which was divided among himself, Li Renguang, and Chen Yaokun, with each receiving RMB 1,500.

4. In 1984, for the foundation works of Employee Dormitories Nos. 84-1 and 84-2 (self-assigned numbers) to be built on Changgang Road by Guangzhou Heavy Machinery Factory, Luo Guoqing introduced the pile-digging team led by Wang Yingquan of Sanshui County Construction Engineering Company to participate in the bidding, and they agreed on a "kickback" of RMB 24,000. Luo Guoqing informed Li Renguang and Chen Yaokun of this situation respectively. In December of the same year, Luo Guoqing collected a "kickback" of RMB 21,500 from Wang Yingquan (RMB 2,500 was unpaid due to Wang's cash shortage), distributing RMB 3,000 to Li Renguang, RMB 2,000 to Chen Yaokun, and keeping RMB 16,500 for himself.

5. In May 1985, the Guangzhou Heavy Machinery Factory adopted an open bid with secret bidding method for the construction of the superstructure works of Project No. 84-1. Luo Guoqing secretly disclosed the winning bid amount to Deng Quanji of the construction team of Sanshui County Construction Engineering Company, enabling that team to win the bid and undertake the project. Luo Guoqing demanded a "kickback" of RMB 75,000 from Deng Quanji, but actually collected RMB 53,000. From this sum, Luo distributed RMB 9,000 to Li Renguang, RMB 8,000 to Chen Yaokun, RMB 4,000 each to Liang Hongjie and Zhao Jilin, and RMB 1,000 to Zhang Mofeng (not prosecuted), a cadre in the same department, keeping RMB 27,000 for himself.

6. In July 1985, the Guangzhou Heavy Machinery Factory adopted a closed bidding method for the superstructure works of Project No. 84-2. Before the bidding, Liang Hongjie conspired with Luo Guoqing, and with Li Renguang's consent, promised to award the project to the Li Bichun Construction Team of the Guangzhou Work Area of Wuchuan County Construction and Installation Engineering Company on condition of a "kickback" of RMB 50,000, and they filled in a bid form. Subsequently, after Luo Guoqing and Liang Hongjie learned the exact base bid from Li Renguang, they engaged in fraud: Liang Hongjie refilled the bid form, which was handed by Luo Guoqing to Li Renguang to secretly replace the original bid form filled by Li Bichun, thereby enabling Li Bichun to win the bid. Liang Hongjie then collected a "kickback" of RMB 36,000 from Li Bichun (RMB 14,000 was not realized), which was distributed by Luo Guoqing as follows: RMB 10,000 to Li Renguang, RMB 6,000 each to Chen Yaokun and Zhao Jilin, and RMB 7,000 each to Liang Hongjie and himself.

7. From 1983 to 1985, Li Renguang assigned the projects for the additional floor of the clinic building and the technical renovation and maintenance works of the Guangzhou Heavy Machinery Factory to the Zhuliao Engineering Team of Guangzhou Suburbs and the No. 208 Construction Team of Panyu County No. 2 Construction Company respectively. He accepted a bribe of RMB 5,000 from the Zhuliao Engineering Team and a bribe of RMB 3,000 from the No. 208 Construction Team.

In addition, Luo Guoqing, Li Renguang, Chen Yaokun, Liang Hongjie, and Zhao Jilin also assigned the factory's Project No. 84-3 to the No. 406 Construction Team of Zhanjiang City No. 4 Construction Engineering Company, and through Li Bichun, agreed with that construction team on a "kickback" of RMB 35,000. However, due to the exposure of the case, the bribe was not realized.

The facts of the bribe-taking by the above-listed defendants are confirmed by witness testimony and documentary evidence. The evidence is reliable and sufficient, and the defendants have also confessed.

The Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province, upon trial of this case, held that Defendants Luo Guoqing, Li Renguang, Chen Yaokun, Liang Hongjie, and Zhao Jilin jointly committed the crime, constituting joint intentional crime as defined in Article 22, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. In the joint crime, Luo Guoqing plotted and directly demanded and accepted bribes, actively distributed the illicit money, and personally received RMB 65,000 in bribes. Li Renguang, as a principal leader of the company, openly decided on the acceptance of bribes by Luo Guoqing and others in the joint crime, and personally received RMB 51,500 in bribes. These two defendants played a principal role in the joint crime and, pursuant to Article 23, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, are the principal offenders in this case and should be severely punished. Chen Yaokun, as one of the company's leaders, participated in the joint bribery and received RMB 24,500 in bribes. Liang Hongjie and Zhao Jilin actively participated in the crime and received bribes of RMB 18,000 and RMB 17,000 respectively. These three defendants played a secondary and auxiliary role in the joint crime and, pursuant to Article 24, Paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Criminal Law, are the accomplices in this case and may be given a lighter punishment as deemed appropriate. All the above defendants were state functionaries in charge of infrastructure construction at a state-owned factory, performing public duties in accordance with the law. After the promulgation of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Severely Punishing Criminals Who Seriously Sabotage the Economy, they exploited their positions, over a period of nearly two years, used the method of collecting "kickbacks," agreed to accept bribes eight times totaling RMB 256,500, and actually accepted bribes of RMB 183,000 (including the RMB 7,000 distributed to Qin Hongtian, Liu Man, Chen Jinbin, and Zhang Mofeng) due to the other parties' temporary shortage of funds or the exposure of the case. Their acts constituted the crime of accepting bribes as defined in Article 185, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law. Luo Guoqing and Li Renguang accepted bribes of a huge amount, and the circumstances were especially serious. Pursuant to Item (2) of Article 1 of the Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Severely Punishing Criminals Who Seriously Sabotage the Economy, those who accept bribes shall be punished by reference to the crime of corruption under Article 155 of the Criminal Law.

Accordingly, on December 18, 1985, the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court sentenced Defendants Luo Guoqing and Li Renguang to life imprisonment for the crime of accepting bribes, and, pursuant to Article 53, Paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law, deprived them of political rights for life; sentenced Defendant Chen Yaokun to 13 years' imprisonment for the crime of accepting bribes; sentenced Defendant Liang Hongjie to 10 years' imprisonment for the crime of accepting bribes; and sentenced Defendant Zhao Jilin to 8 years' imprisonment for the crime of accepting bribes. Pursuant to Article 60 of the Criminal Law, it was ordered that the illicit money and property surrendered by Luo Guoqing, Li Renguang, Chen Yaokun, Liang Hongjie, and Zhao Jilin be confiscated.

After the judgment was pronounced, Li Renguang appealed to the Guangdong High People's Court on the ground that the circumstances of his crime were not especially serious; Liang Hongjie appealed on the ground that he had reported others' crimes and requested a mitigated punishment; and Zhao Jilin appealed on the ground that he had not actively participated in the crime.

After accepting the case, the Guangdong High People's Court, pursuant to Article 134, Paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, reviewed the entire case. Upon trial, it held that the appellants Li Renguang, Liang Hongjie, and Zhao Jilin, and the co-defendants in the same case Luo Guoqing and Chen Yaokun, as enterprise leading cadres and engineering technical personnel, exploited their positions to demand project "kickbacks" from construction units and accepted bribes totaling RMB 183,000. Li Renguang was a principal leader of the company, played a principal role in the joint crime, and was one of the principal offenders in this case. Moreover, the amount of bribes he accepted was huge, and the circumstances were especially serious. His appeal was clearly unfounded and was not accepted. Liang Hongjie and Zhao Jilin were key engineering technical personnel who actively participated in the crime and should be severely punished according to law. Although Liang Hongjie reported several criminal leads of others after the case was exposed, upon verification, some of the issues he reported were unfounded, and none constituted circumstances for a mitigated punishment, so his appeal was not accepted. Zhao Jilin's denial of active participation in the crime was clearly unfounded and was not accepted. The original trial judgment found the facts of the crimes of the appellants and co-defendants to be clear, the evidence reliable and sufficient, the application of law correct, and the trial procedure lawful. On March 22, 1986, pursuant to Item (1) of Article 136 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the court ruled to reject the appeals of Li Renguang, Liang Hongjie, and Zhao Jilin and affirm the original judgment.
